feedback.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=x(t)+3y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=3x(t)+y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear differential equations above. The eigenvalues of the system's matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=4$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-2,$ for which the corresponding eigenvectors are ${v}_{1}=[1,\text{ }1]^{T}$ and ${v}_{2}=[-1,\text{ }1]^{T},$ respectively. Select the correct options below regarding the given system.$\,$
{{field-1}} is {{field-2}} line.

$\,$
$y=-x$ is {{field-3}} line.

$\,$
The equilibrium point (origin) is {{field-4}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
The general solution of the system is

$$
[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]={c}_{1}{e}^{4t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}{e}^{-2t}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

- The line that passes through the origin and is parallel to ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ has the equation 

$$
y=x.
$$

The straight-line solutions of the form
${c}_{1}{e}^{4t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$
lie on that line and approach infinity as $t\to \infty .$ So, $y=x$ is $\text{an unstable}$ line.

- The line that passes through the origin and is parallel to ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ has the equation 

$$
y=-x.
$$

The straight-line solutions of the form
${c}_{2}{e}^{-2t}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$
lie on that line and approach the origin as $t\to \infty .$ So, $y=-x$ is $\text{a stable}$ line.

Therefore, the equilibrium point (origin) is $\text{a saddle point}.$
